case_title: Rajput Jabbarsingh Malaji v. State of Gujarat
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (unspecified; the witness said 'they all are related')
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302; Bombay Police Act s.135(1)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (wife), res gestae witnesses, medical (postmortem), recovery of scarf and axe, forensic serology (FSL report)
aggravating_circumstances: Single very hard blow to the face with an axe causing instantaneous death, as found by the Court
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302 and sentenced to life imprisonment with fine of Rs. 500 (default 3 months RI); convicted under Bombay Police Act s.135(1) with 4 months simple imprisonment and fine of Rs. 100 (default 15 days); sentences concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 597 of 1998) dismissed; conviction and sentence upheld
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 (appeal dismissed in full; the Court's analysis addresses s.302 only)
neutral_facts: Late on the night of the incident, at about 2 a.m., the victim was asleep on a cot outside the family home, with his wife and their small child of about one and a half years on a nearby cot. The wife raised shouts for help. Family members, including the victim's brother who later lodged the complaint, rushed to the spot and found the victim with severe facial injuries and bleeding heavily. The victim was taken by tractor to a hospital, where he was declared dead on arrival. The complaint lodged that night stated that an unidentified person had assaulted the victim with an axe and run away. Later, after the wife had become somewhat composed, she told the victim's two brothers that the accused had struck her husband on the face with an axe. The brothers said that, while entering the field earlier, they had also seen the accused going away with an axe in hand. Their statements were recorded by police soon after. The wife stated that she woke to painful shrieks, saw the accused standing with an axe, and recognised the accused in the light of an electric bulb that was already lit. The postmortem doctor described a fatal injury to the face inflicted by an axe. During investigation, the accused made disclosure statements leading to recovery of a blood-stained scarf and a blood-stained axe. Forensic serological analysis found human blood of group O, the victim's blood group, on the articles, including the accused's scarf and the axe.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from severe axe wounds to the face
number_of_offences: 2 charged; 2 finally upheld (appeal dismissed in full; the Court's analysis addresses s.302 IPC only)
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of the wife (eyewitness); testimony of the two brothers as res gestae witnesses; postmortem evidence of PW-1; FSL serological report; recovery of blood-stained scarf and axe on the accused's disclosure
witness_credibility: Court found the wife's evidence and the brothers' evidence mutually corroborated, of sterling quality, and no reason to implicate the accused falsely
post_offence_conduct: Disclosure statements in police custody leading to recovery of blood-stained scarf and axe
trial_duration: offence: 2/3.04.1994 (intervening night); trial judgment: 07.03.1998; High Court: 28/29.4.2005; Supreme Court: 24.05.2011
legal_representation: Accused: S. Usha Reddy. State: Kamaldeep Dayal, Hemantika Wahi, Suveni Banerjee
investigation_status: FIR registered on complaint; investigation completed with recoveries, postmortem and FSL analysis; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted, life imprisonment. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction affirmed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
defence_argument: Not stated; the judgment says only that the appellant challenged the conviction on a variety of grounds, without specifying them
legal_principle_applied: Res gestae under s.6 Evidence Act; concurrent findings of the two lower courts not to be interfered with absent good reason; guilt proved beyond shadow of any doubt
